question: Filtered water turbidity rises slowly over several days while raw water quality is steady and chemical doses are unchanged. What is the best first troubleshooting step?
correctAnswer: Compare filter run data, head loss and backwash records to see which filter changed first
explanation: A single filter drifting first points to a unit problem such as a poor backwash or media issue, while a plant wide change would affect all filters together.
options: Compare filter run data, head loss and backwash records to see which filter changed first
Increase the coagulant dose for the whole plant at once
Take the clearwell out of service for inspection
Replace all filter media on the same day
sourceTitle: US EPA - Surface Water Treatment Rule Turbidity Guidance Manual
sourceReference: Supporting resource category: Advanced process troubleshooting. See SOURCES.md: these are not claim-level verification citations.
optionA: Compare filter run data, head loss and backwash records to see which filter changed first
optionB: Increase the coagulant dose for the whole plant at once
optionC: Take the clearwell out of service for inspection
optionD: Replace all filter media on the same day

Drain and refill the chlorine contact tank
